drops, prepare writes its explanation with git's prefix, in a paragraph of
  its own between the user's lines and the trailer, so a line typed just
  above the trailer cannot join the subject paragraph. Any other message gets
  no explanation, because git would record it and the prompt it quotes: one
  git does not open, and one under `whitespace`, `verbatim` or `scissors`
  cleanup. Commit-msg judges an emptied message by the same editor signal,
  prefix and scissors line.
- **Stamp.** Prepare records each trailer it stamps (an ID it generates, a
  session's reserved one, or the one an amend restores) in the per-worktree
  git dir until the next post-commit (`recordStampedTrailer`). Any other ID
  in the final block (pasted, reused with `commit -C`, typed in the editor) is
  a link only: prepare stamps its own trailer after it, and post-commit
  creates a checkpoint only for a trailer prepare stamped
  (`pickCondensationTarget`). Without a stamp (an amend keeping its trailer,
  a sequence operation) post-commit condenses only into the last trailer
  whose checkpoint exists, and only for the session that owns it
  (`stampedByAnotherCommit`), so a teammate's checkpoint this clone has not
  fetched is never created with local work.
- **Moved trailers.** A trailer the user's edits move out of the final
  block, such as a body typed below it or the line commented out under a
  cleanup mode that keeps comment lines, no longer links the commit.
  Post-commit, attach and `explain` agree: the commit is treated as one whose
  trailer the user removed, and `entire attach` can link it.

  listing, the export and the review re-run guard show the checkpoint attach
  and `--generate` use (`CommitCheckpoint`), falling back to the first ID
  anywhere only when the final block names none. `explain --checkpoint`
  lists a commit under every ID that view reads from it

  read-only

  the whole message, because squash commits carry their squashed commits'
  trailers in the body.

package integration

// Only a commit's final trailer block links it to a checkpoint. A checkpoint ID
// anywhere else in the message (pasted, quoted, or left over from another
// commit) names a checkpoint the commit did not stamp, so the hooks must stamp
// a fresh trailer and condense the session's work there.

)

func TestTrailerAuthority_BodyLineNamingUnknownCheckpoint(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t)
	authorityAgentTurn(env, "mine.txt", "my agent work\n")

	_, final := advCommit(env,
		"Fix the bug\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: "+advForeignCheckpoint+"\n\nSigned-off-by: Test User <test@example.com>\n",
		"message", keepAll, "mine.txt")

	stamped := requireFreshFinalTrailer(t, final, advForeignCheckpoint)
	require.True(t, advCheckpointStored(env, stamped), "the session's work belongs in the checkpoint prepare stamped")
	require.False(t, advCheckpointStored(env, advForeignCheckpoint),
		"a body line must not claim a checkpoint ID this clone does not have")
}

func TestTrailerAuthority_IndentedLineNamingUnknownCheckpoint(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t)
	authorityAgentTurn(env, "mine.txt", "my agent work\n")

	_, final := advCommit(env, "Fix the bug\n\n  Entire-Checkpoint: "+advForeignCheckpoint+"\n",
		"message", keepAll, "mine.txt")

	stamped := requireFreshFinalTrailer(t, final, advForeignCheckpoint)
	require.True(t, advCheckpointStored(env, stamped), "the session's work belongs in the checkpoint prepare stamped")
	require.False(t, advCheckpointStored(env, advForeignCheckpoint),
		"an indented line is not a trailer, so it must not claim a checkpoint ID")
}

func TestTrailerAuthority_BodyLineNamingExistingCheckpoint(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t)
	authorityAgentTurn(env, "first.txt", "first change\n")
	env.GitCommitWithHooks("First change", "first.txt")
	existing := env.GetCheckpointIDFromCommitMessage(env.GetHeadHash())
	require.NotEmpty(t, existing, "precondition: the first commit is linked")
	before, ok := checkpointBlob(env, existing, paths.MetadataFileName)
	require.True(t, ok, "precondition: the first checkpoint is stored")

	authorityAgentTurn(env, "second.txt", "second change\n")
	_, final := advCommit(env,
		"Follow-up\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: "+existing+"\n\nSigned-off-by: Test User <test@example.com>\n",
		"message", keepAll, "second.txt")

	stamped := requireFreshFinalTrailer(t, final, existing)
	require.True(t, advCheckpointStored(env, stamped), "the follow-up commit gets a checkpoint of its own")
	after, ok := checkpointBlob(env, existing, paths.MetadataFileName)
	require.True(t, ok)
	require.Equal(t, before, after, "the checkpoint the body mentions must not change")
}

Good, #8 is closed, and #9 is resolved for the normal path too -- in the amend case, prepare keeps the message while post-commit falls back to the last existing trailer, which stays consistent. For #1, I'm now closing it against corruption, but flagging that in the -C/-c/--amend case with a foreign trailer, the session's work ends up unlinked since prepare stamps a fresh one; I should note that the finding now specifically calls out that the -C path drops the session link. Next I want to think through the concurrency race further.

Walking through the race case: two commits A and B in the same worktree, where A's prepare writes F_A and its post-commit hook fires, calling takeStampedTrailers which removes the record file once it finds the trailer. If B's prepare writes F_B into that record before A's post-commit takes it, A will sweep up both F_A and F_B and remove the file, leaving B's post-commit with nothing to find for F_B, so B's session work goes uncondensed and its trailer dangles. But if B's prepare reads the file before A removes it and writes afterward, B ends up with the combined {F_A, F_B} and everything works. So the bad interleaving is real and timing-dependent. I'm also noting a secondary issue -- A's post-commit might observe B's commit via repo.Head() if B finishes first, though B's commit path (prepare plus editor/message plus commit) takes long enough that it would need to complete within A's post-commit window for that to happen.

I'm marking this as a low-severity, plausible but unverified race, since it requires a fast prepare with minimal content to stamp. I also consider whether recordStampedTrailer and takeStampedTrailers, which operate without locking, could race across worktree boundaries if a tool uses an alternate GIT_INDEX_FILE bypassing the shared index.lock serialization -- this seems like an edge case worth flagging but not critical. I think I have enough findings now and want to verify the claim about no git process being added, then double-check the squashedCommits logic.

Checking the ordering between squashedCommits and stripInheritedCheckpointTrailers for the squash case -- when SQUASH_MSG has trailers but no readable commits, the new behavior returns without stripping, which seems harmless since indented lines aren't parsed as trailers anyway. But I notice a real edge case: squashedCommits parses any line starting with "commit <sha>" even if it's indented body text from a different commit's message, like a revert commit saying "This reverts commit <sha>" -- that could get misidentified as a squashed commit line, though the field count might not match.

This means a squashed commit whose message body happens to quote a line like "commit <full-sha>" (plausible if someone pastes git log output) could cause that referenced commit's trailers to get inherited unintentionally. It's a new, low-severity vector since previously these IDs only came from matched text in the squash context, not from parsed commit bodies.

The fix would be to require matching lines to have no leading whitespace, since squash message headers are unindented while body content is indented four spaces. I want to verify this with a quick overlay test — setting up a repo with a base commit and a commit Q on main that includes a trailer, then testing whether squashing picks it up incorrectly.

That's odd — the squash would wrongly link to Q's checkpoint even though Q's work isn't actually part of the squashed changes, since Q is already on main. I should test this case directly.

## Review of 5953fa815..8246fe044 (7 commits)

I didn't change the worktree. Every probe ran through `go test -overlay` from scratchpad files, and the worktree's git dir has no leftover stamped-trailers file. The full `strategy` and `trailers` unit suites pass at 8246fe044.

### Confirmed issues

**1. `git commit -C <sha>`, `-c`, and `--amend` of a commit with a foreign trailer leave the session's work unlinked. Severity: medium.**
- **Where:** `manual_commit_hooks.go:464` sends source `commit` (which covers -c, -C and --amend) to `handleAmendCommitMsg`. That function returns at `:864-876` whenever the final block has any live trailer, so prepare never stamps a fresh one.
- **What happens:** post-commit finds `ids=[X]`, an empty stamped set, and no X in the store, so it returns `found=false`.
- **Scenario:** a teammate's commit carries `Entire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6`, which this clone hasn't fetched. An agent turn writes `mine.txt`, then `git commit -C <teammate-sha>`. The commit records `"Teammate change\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6\n"`, no checkpoint is created, and the agent's work in that commit has no link. `--amend --no-edit` on the teammate commit gives the same result.
- **Contradiction:** the 2515903c3 commit message ("any other final-block ID gets a fresh trailer after it") and the doc (`sessions-and-checkpoints.md:337-341`: "reused with `commit -C` ... prepare stamps its own trailer after it") both say otherwise.
- **Why tests miss it:** `TestTrailerAuthority_ReusedMessageNamingUnfetchedCheckpoint` only asserts that the foreign ID isn't created.
- **Verified:** two overlay integration probes, for -C and for amend. Both fail on "session work linked".

**2. Squash inheritance now follows `commit <sha>` lines quoted in a squashed commit's body. Severity: low. This is new in 8e4b45d66 and is the same kind of bug as finding #3.**
- **Where:** `squashedCommits` (`manual_commit_hooks.go:758-766`) accepts any line whose fields are `commit <hash>`, including the message lines SQUASH_MSG indents by 4 spaces. Inherited IDs now come from the final blocks of those parsed commits.
- **Scenario:** a feature commit's body contains `commit <sha of an older main commit>`, then `merge --squash feature`. The squash inherits the main commit's checkpoint.
- **Verified:** overlay unit probe. Inherited `[…J51 (real), …J50 (quoted main commit)]`, and both were written into the final block. Before this commit, IDs came from the SQUASH_MSG text, which doesn't contain J50.
- **Fix:** accept only unindented `commit ` header lines.

**3. `explain --checkpoint` no longer lists GitHub squash-merge commits (or older local squash commits) under most of their squashed checkpoints. Severity: low to medium, read-only.**
- **Where:** `explain.go:1697` now matches through `CommitCheckpoints` (`manual_commit_provenance.go:86`).
- **Verified:** probe on a GitHub-style message (`Title (#42)\n\n* First\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: A\n\n* Second\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: B`):
  - plain message: `CommitCheckpoints=[B]`
  - with GitHub's `---------\n\nCo-authored-by:` footer: `[A]`
  - before the change, both A and B listed the commit.
- **Effect:** once the PR branch is gone, N-1 of the N squashed checkpoints show no commit on main. This conflicts with the doc's own reason why the other read-only lookups still scan the whole message.

**4. Several existing PostCommit tests now pass without testing anything. Severity: test strength.**
- **Cause:** these tests commit an unstamped trailer for an ID the store lacks. PostCommit now returns at `!found` before reaching the logic they pin.
- **Affected tests:**
  - `phase_postcommit_test.go:2653` (`runEndedLingeringRecordNotCondensed`). Its own comment says the trailer is there to get past the early bail.
  - `phase_postcommit_test.go:1978` (IdleSessionEmptyFilesTouched)
  - `phase_postcommit_test.go:2046` (NoTranscriptFallback)
  - `phase_postcommit_test.go:2232` (second commit of FullyCondensedEnded)
  - `trackable_paths_test.go:66` (DropsPathsInsideSubmodule; its sibling at line 36 was given a stamp, this one wasn't)
  - `session_identity_test.go:494` (guest commit)
- **Verified on `TestPostCommit_TaskRecordCondensationScope`:**
  - I broke `idleWithLiveTaskRecord` so it trusts ENDED lingering records. The shipped test still passes.
  - The same break plus `recordStampedTrailer` added to the test makes it fail.
- **Production behavior is fine:** with stamps added, all six pass on the current code.
- **Also affected:** the hookperf test (`commit_hook_perf_test.go:118-126`) injects an unstamped trailer, so it now times a PostCommit that does nothing.

### Plausible, not run (both low)
- **Race between commits in one worktree:** git releases index.lock before post-commit. Commit B's prepare can append F_B to the record before commit A's post-commit runs `takeStampedTrailers` (`manual_commit_provenance.go:305`), which removes the whole file. B's post-commit then sees no stamp, so F_B is a dangling trailer and B's work isn't condensed.
- **Silent fail-closed:** if `recordStampedTrailer` cannot write (`:288` logs only at Debug), prepare has stamped a trailer that post-commit will now never create. Before, post-commit condensed into it anyway.

### Tests
- **New tests:** each one I checked would fail without its fix.
- **Rewritten tests:** `TestStampedTrailer_OnlyTrailersPrepareStamped`, `TestPickCondensationTarget` and the amend!-fixup test reflect the intended new behavior and aren't weaker. The removed "recheck" test no longer applies, since the target's existence is now read once.

### Findings 1-9 not fully closed
- **#1:** the foreign ID is no longer written, but the `-C` and amend cases now record the commit with no link to the session's work (issue 1).
- **#2:** only partly closed. A commit whose final block names no checkpoint is still listed under a checkpoint its body merely mentions; `TestGetAssociatedCommits_BodyMentionIsNotALink` pins "See Entire-Checkpoint: X for context." as listed. The fix also drops the squash-merge listings (issue 3).
- **#3:** whole-message scans are gone, but quoted `commit <sha>` lines turn body content into links again (issue 2).
- **#4, #5, #7, #8, #9:** closed.
